title: Linearization of square-zero lifts to an arbitrary algebraic space
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ a first order thickening of $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with ideal $\mathcal J$. Regard $\mathcal J$ as a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-modules, since $\mathcal J^2=0$, on the small etale site of $T_0$. Write $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ for the relative differential module on the small etale site of $X$, representing $S$-derivations of its structure sheaf. Module sheaves are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; pullback $g^*M$ means $\mathcal O_{T_0}\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O_X}g^{-1}M$. Fix an $S$-map $a:T\to X$, put $a_0=aj$, and set $L_X(a_0)=\{b:T\to X\text{ over }S\mid bj=a_0\}$. There is a canonical bijection
$$\delta_a:L_X(a_0)\xrightarrow{\sim} M_X(a_0):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(a_0^*\Omega^1_{X/S},\mathcal J).$$
It sends $a$ to zero. Under the derivation interpretation, $\delta_a(b)$ is $b^\sharp-a^\sharp$, on the etale sites identified along $j$; its inverse replaces $a^\sharp$ by $a^\sharp+D$. For every $S$-morphism $u:X\to Y$ of algebraic spaces, postcomposition obeys
$$\delta_{ua}(ub)=u_*\delta_a(b),$$
where $u_*:M_X(a_0)\to M_Y(ua_0)$ is the $\Gamma(T_0,\mathcal O_{T_0})$-linear map taking a relative derivation $D$ to $D\circ u^\sharp$. These maps satisfy $(v\circ u)_*=v_*\circ u_*$ and $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*=\mathrm{id}$. No local finite presentation, smoothness, affineness, or group structure is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), and 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with the target thickening X in X. Naturality under postcomposition is the chain rule for the difference of ring-sheaf maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-first-order-ringed-description] to $T_0\hookrightarrow T$. Work on the common small etale topos, with exact sequence $0\to\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_T\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal O_{T_0}\to0$. The $\mathcal O_T$-action on $\mathcal J$ factors through $q$, since two lifts of a scalar differ by a section of $\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal J^2=0$. By the maps clause of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization], applied over $S$ to source thickening $T_0\subset T$ and trivial target thickening $X\subset X$, the lifts $b$ correspond exactly to maps of ring sheaves $\beta:a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_T$ over $S$ with $q\beta=a_0^\sharp$. In particular all their ring maps have the same inverse-image functor. Put $A=a_0^\sharp$ and $\alpha=a^\sharp$, so $q\alpha=A$.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening X in X

proof.text:
For a lift $b$, put $D=\beta-\alpha$. The equality $q\beta=q\alpha$ makes $D$ uniquely a map into the kernel $\mathcal J$. On local sections $x,y$ of $a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X$, expansion of $\beta(x)\beta(y)=(\alpha(x)+D(x))(\alpha(y)+D(y))$ gives
$$D(xy)=A(x)D(y)+A(y)D(x),$$
because $D(x)D(y)=0$ and the action factors through $q$. Additivity follows by subtraction, and $D$ vanishes on the inverse image of the base ring because both maps are over $S$. Thus it is a relative derivation. These equalities are identities of sheaf maps: subtraction and multiplication commute with every restriction.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening X in X

proof.text: Identify these derivations with $M_X(a_0)$. By [lem-trf-topos-inverse-image-differentials], $a_0^{-1}\Omega^1_{X/S}$ represents differentials of $a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ relative to the inverse image of the base ring; the universal derivation property on sheaves is [lem-trf-sheafified-module-differentials-cokernel]. For the $a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal J$ acted on through $A$, a derivation therefore gives a unique linear map $\ell:a_0^{-1}\Omega^1_{X/S}\to\mathcal J$. It gives a unique $\mathcal O_{T_0}$-linear map from $a_0^*\Omega^1_{X/S}=\mathcal O_{T_0}\otimes_{a_0^{-1}\mathcal O_X}a_0^{-1}\Omega^1_{X/S}$ by $t\otimes\omega\mapsto t\ell(\omega)$. Conversely restrict such a map to $1\otimes\omega$ and compose with the universal derivation. The tensor balancing relation proves these operations well-defined and inverse. This is the tensor pullback adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Define $\delta_a(b)$ to be this homomorphism.

Conversely take $m\in M_X(a_0)$ and its derivation $D$ from step 3. Define $\beta=\alpha+D$, with $D$ included into $\mathcal O_T$. It is additive and unital ($D(1)=0$), agrees with $\alpha$ on base scalars, and satisfies
$$\beta(x)\beta(y)=\alpha(x)\alpha(y)+\alpha(x)D(y)+\alpha(y)D(x)=\alpha(xy)+D(xy)=\beta(xy).$$
Here the missing quadratic term is zero by $\mathcal J^2=0$. Also $q\beta=A$. The maps clause of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization] now gives a unique $S$-map $b:T\to X$ with $bj=a_0$ and $b^\sharp=\beta$. It applies to the trivial target thickening, whose zero ideal is square-zero; it imposes no presentation or smoothness hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening X in X

proof.text: Starting with $b$, the constructed inverse has ring map $\alpha+(b^\sharp-\alpha)=b^\sharp$, hence is $b$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-ringed-realization]. Starting with $m$, subtraction from $\alpha+D$ returns $D$, and the mutually inverse universal-derivation and tensor correspondences of step 3 return $m$. Thus $\delta_a$ is a bijection with the specified inverse. Its value at $a$ is zero since $a^\sharp-a^\sharp=0$.

source.place: Tags 0618 (lemma-difference-derivation), 0619 (equation-D), 04D0 (lemma-action-by-derivations), with trivial target thickening X in X

proof.text:
For $u:X\to Y$ pull $u^\sharp$ back to the common topos of $T_0$ and $T$. The formula for a composite ring map gives
$$(ub)^\sharp-(ua)^\sharp=(b^\sharp-a^\sharp)\circ a_0^{-1}u^\sharp.$$
Precomposition preserves additivity, Leibniz relative to $(ua_0)^\sharp$, and vanishing on the base. Hence step 3 identifies the right side with the stated $u_*\delta_a(b)$. For $t\in\Gamma(T_0,\mathcal O_{T_0})$ and derivations $D,E$, evaluating at any local section $y$ gives $(D+E)(u^\sharp y)=D(u^\sharp y)+E(u^\sharp y)$ and $(tD)(u^\sharp y)=tD(u^\sharp y)$; so $u_*$ is linear. Precomposition with the identity does nothing, and associativity of composition gives $D\circ u^\sharp\circ v^\sharp$ for both $(vu)_*(D)$ and $v_*u_*(D)$. The representing correspondences are injective, so these equalities of derivations prove all stated equalities in $M$.
